citations.title: E-commerce grievance officer: acknowledge in 48 hours, resolve in one month
citations.plain: Every e-commerce platform must have a grievance officer. That officer must acknowledge your complaint within 48 hours and resolve it within one month of receiving it. Sellers on marketplaces must also appoint a grievance officer with the same timelines (rule 6(4)(b)).

citations.title: Limitation period for filing complaint
citations.plain: You must file a consumer complaint within two years from the date the problem (cause of action) arose. A later complaint can still be accepted if you show sufficient cause for the delay, but the Commission must record its reasons for condoning the delay.

citations.title: Reliefs the District Commission can order
citations.plain: If your complaint is proved, the Commission can order the seller or service provider to remove defects, replace the goods, refund the price or charges with interest, pay compensation for loss or injury (including punitive damages), stop the unfair practice, withdraw hazardous goods, issue corrective advertisements, and pay your costs.

deadlines.note: The commission can accept a late complaint only if you show sufficient cause for the delay.

draft.title: Consumer Complaint against Online Shopping App for Non‑Refund of Returned Phone
draft.body_markdown:
BEFORE THE DISTRICT CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION, [[FILL: district]]

**Complainant:**
Name: [[FILL: Your Full Name]]
Address: [[FILL: Your Full Residential Address]]
Phone: [[FILL: Your Mobile Number]]
Email: [[FILL: Your Email Address]]

**Opposite Party:**
Name: [[FILL: Online Shopping App Name]]
Address: [[FILL: Registered Office/Corporate Address of the App]]
Phone: [[FILL: Customer Care Number of the App]]
Email: [[FILL: Official Customer Care Email]]

**COMPLAINT UNDER SECTION 35 OF THE CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT, 2019**

1. I am a consumer within the meaning of **CPA2019‑S2‑7** as I purchased a mobile phone through the online shopping app and paid Rs 18,499.
2. On **10 September 2026** I returned the phone (order ID **OD12345**) and the pickup was completed as per the app’s return policy.
3. The amount paid for the phone was **Rs 18,499**.
4. I raised a refund request immediately after the return. The app’s grievance officer repeatedly assured me that the refund was “under process”.
5. I lodged four separate tickets with the app’s support team; the last ticket (Ticket No. [[FILL: Ticket Number]]) was raised on **1 October 2026** and still no refund has been credited to my bank account.
6. I possess the following evidence: order ID **OD12345**, ticket numbers and dates, and chat screenshots showing the “refund under process” messages.
7. I have not received any official receipt of the return or any written acknowledgment from the app confirming the return or the pending refund.

**Deficiency in Service / Unfair Trade Practice**
The app has failed to refund the amount paid for the returned phone despite completing the pickup and acknowledging the return. This constitutes a *deficiency* in service under **CPA2019‑S2‑11** and amounts to an *unfair trade practice* under **CPA2019‑S2‑47** as the app misleads the consumer by repeatedly assuring a refund that is never effected.

**Jurisdiction**
- The cause of action arose in **Jaipur, Rajasthan**, where I reside and where the return was effected. 
- The amount in dispute (Rs 18,499) falls within the jurisdiction of the District Commission as per **CPJURIS2021‑R3‑5** (limit up to Rs 50 lakh).
- The complaint is filed within the statutory period of two years from the date the problem arose (**1 October 2026**) in accordance with **CPA2019‑S69**.

**Reliefs Prayed For**
1. Refund of the full amount of **Rs 18,499** with interest at the prevailing bank rate from the date of the last ticket (1 Oct 2026) until actual payment.
2. Compensation of **Rs 5,000** for mental harassment and inconvenience caused by the undue delay.
3. Reimbursement of any costs incurred in filing this complaint, including the nominal filing fee (nil as per **CPCDRC2020‑R7**).
4. Any other relief that the Hon’ble Commission may deem just and proper.

**List of Documents Annexed**
1. Copy of the order confirmation and payment receipt (if available).
2. Copy of the return pickup acknowledgment (if any).
3. Screenshots of chat conversations showing “refund under process”.
4. Copies of all four ticket numbers and dates.
5. Copy of this complaint.

**Verification**
I, [[FILL: Your Full Name]], the complainant above, do hereby verify that the contents of this complaint are true to the best of my knowledge and belief, and that no material fact has been concealed.

Date: [[FILL: Date of filing]]
Place: Jaipur

Signature of Complainant

---

citations.title: Who is a 'consumer'
citations.plain: You are a consumer if you buy goods or hire/avail a service for payment (paid, promised, or in instalments), including online, teleshopping, direct selling or multi-level marketing. People who use the goods or service with the buyer's approval are also covered. Buying for resale or a commercial purpose is excluded, but buying something to earn your own livelihood through self-employment is not treated as commercial.

citations.title: Meaning of 'deficiency' in service
citations.plain: A deficiency is any fault, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature or manner of a service that the law or a contract requires. It also covers negligence or acts or omissions that cause you loss, and deliberately withholding relevant information from you.

citations.title: Meaning of 'unfair trade practice'
citations.plain: An unfair trade practice is any unfair method or unfair or deceptive practice used to promote the sale, use or supply of goods or services. Examples listed in the Act include false claims about standard, quality, quantity or grade of goods (oral, written, visual or electronic).

citations.title: Who can file a complaint, and electronic filing
citations.plain: A complaint can be filed with the District Commission by the consumer, by a registered consumer association, by one or more consumers on behalf of many with the same interest (with the Commission's permission), or by the Central/State Government or the Central Authority. The Act allows complaints to be filed electronically, and the prescribed fee can be paid electronically.

citations.title: Limitation period for filing complaint
citations.plain: You must file a consumer complaint within two years from the date the problem (cause of action) arose. A later complaint can still be accepted if you show sufficient cause for the delay, but the Commission must record its reasons for condoning the delay.

citations.act: Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission, the State Commission and the National Commission) Rules, 2021
citations.title: Money limits of District, State and National Commissions
citations.plain: Where you file depends on how much you paid for the goods or service. Up to Rs 50 lakh: District Commission. Above Rs 50 lakh and up to Rs 2 crore: State Commission. Above Rs 2 crore: National Commission (NCDRC).

citations.act: Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) Rules, 2020
citations.title: Complaint filing fee schedule (nil up to Rs 5 lakh)
citations.plain: There is no fee for a consumer complaint where the amount paid is up to Rs 5 lakh. The fee is Rs 200 for Rs 5-10 lakh, Rs 400 for Rs 10-20 lakh, Rs 1,000 for Rs 20-50 lakh, Rs 2,000 for Rs 50 lakh-1 crore and Rs 2,500 for Rs 1-2 crore. It rises to Rs 7,500 above Rs 10 crore.

send_instructions: 1. Register on the e‑Jagriti portal (https://e-jagriti.gov.in/) and select ‘File a Complaint’.
2. Fill in the details as per the draft, upload the annexed documents and the chat screenshots as evidence.
3. Pay the filing fee (nil for amounts up to Rs 5 lakh) and submit the complaint electronically.
4. After submission, download the acknowledgement receipt (PDF) and keep it safe as proof of filing.
5. If the opposite party does not respond within 30 days, file a follow‑up application on e‑Jagriti requesting the Commission to issue a notice.
